desc: Ideation: perimeter mapping, answer<=side lemma for k>=4, greedy feasibility plan
Proof sketch: for d <= side, Manhattan >= d iff circular perimeter gap >= d (same/adjacent edges give equality; opposite edges give both >= side); answer <= side via one-point-per-side contradiction
Implement the complete solution: to_t mapping, sort, duplicated array, two-pointer nxt, feasible(d) with all-starts greedy + wrap check, binary search over [0, min(side, 4*side//k)]
Verify against the three provided examples (expect 2, 1, 1)

Stress test vs brute-force subsets for tiny side (2..4), random boundary points, all valid k, including opposite-side midpoint cases where perimeter distance differs from Manhattan — all passed, zero mismatches

Edge cases: all-corners and one-edge clusters covered by exhaustive side=2 testing; wraparound (t near 0 / near 4*side) covered by circular duplicated-array design and random tests; k=25 and side=10^9 are performance-only concerns, addressed by the O(log(side) * n * k) ≈ 12M-op complexity bound with Python big ints avoiding overflow
